blurb: Original medium-sized Schnauzer from southern Germany, with a bristly beard and whiskers
description: The Standard Schnauzer is a medium-sized German working dog with a hard, wiry salt-and-pepper or black coat and a bristly beard; once a farm ratter.
answer: The Standard Schnauzer, or Mittelschnauzer, is a German breed in the Pinscher and Schnauzer group, developed in southern Germany from the 1880s. It is a robust, square, medium-sized dog of about 45 to 50 cm with a bristly beard and whiskers. It is one of three Schnauzer breeds, alongside the Giant and the Miniature.

body: The Schnauzer shares its history with the German Pinscher: rough- and smooth-haired dogs of the same lineage kept as stable dogs and ratters, with both types sometimes in one litter. In 1879 a dog named Schnautzer won the Wire-haired Pinscher class at Hanover. The rough-haired breed was officially renamed Schnauzer in 1917, and the FCI definitively accepted it in 1955. It is now rare in Germany, where the pepper-and-salt variety has been listed as endangered. A Standard Schnauzer won Best in Show at Westminster in 1997.

It stands about 45 to 50 cm, with weight given as 14 to 20 kg or 15 to 24 kg. The coat is hard, wiry and dense over a thick, soft undercoat, in salt-and-pepper or black. Salt-and-pepper ranges from pale silver-grey to dark iron-grey, always with a darker mask. The beard and whiskers are usually lighter than the coat, and the V-shaped ears hang close to the face.

The source text gives little detail on temperament. It is described as a dog of working or utility type with a particular aptitude for ratting, and in the twenty-first century it is commonly kept as a companion.
Sources give little specific detail on care. As a medium-sized working breed it is generally thought to need regular daily exercise, and its wiry coat needs routine grooming.

Median lifespan is reported to be 13 years, slightly above the 12.5-year median for all dogs. The source text names no specific conditions; breed clubs generally recommend health screening of breeding stock and regular veterinary check-ups.

faq.q: How big does a Standard Schnauzer get?
faq.a: It usually stands 45 to 50 cm at the withers and weighs about 14 to 20 kg.

faq.q: How long do Standard Schnauzers live?
faq.a: Median lifespan is reported to be 13 years.

faq.q: What colours do Standard Schnauzers come in?
faq.a: Salt-and-pepper or black. Salt-and-pepper dogs always have a darker mask.

faq.q: Is the Standard Schnauzer recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. It was definitively accepted in 1955 and is FCI breed number 182 in Group 2.
